messages.subject: Error: Object 'stms' not found
messages.body_plain:
Hi All

I've installed the latest QCA version but have been getting errors when I used functions like pof, truthTable, and minimize. To illustrate the errors, I've generated a dummy dataset as attached. Appreciate if anyone can explain why I'm getting these errors.

> conds<-subset(dummy.data[2:7])
> pof(conds,dummy.data$outcome)

Error: Object 'stms' not found.

> ttdummy<-truthTable(dummy.data,outcome = "outcome",
+                     conditions = "x1,x2,x3,x4,x5,x6",
+                     n.cut=1,incl.cut = 0.8,show.cases=T,
+                     sort.by <http://sort.by>="out",decreasing=TRUE)

Below are the results of  print (version) and sessionInfo ( ):

messages.subject: Looking for Director Reserach, strong on QCA, willing to work in Addis, Ethiopia (up to 5 years)
messages.subject_clean: Looking for Director Reserach, strong on QCA, willing to work in Addis, Ethiopia (up to 5 years)
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
I've worked for many years to get the US Goverment's USAID to take QCA further and these efforts are starting to pay off. Specifically, USAID would know like to embedd QCA as the main driver of adaptivement management of a very large household resileince project in the Highlands of Ethiopia. The project is for 5 years. We need a Director of Research and Learning who is strong in QCA to join our team on this opportunity.
The job description is here: https://jobs.socha.net/director-of-research-and-learning-ethiopia/
If you feel you meet the requirements, please apply as well as feel free to refer this opportunity to others who may be eligible.
Thank you,
Carroll Patterson, PhD

messages.subject: Re: Error: Object 'stms' not found
messages.body_plain:
Hmm... the R version should not matter (I have 4.1.0 and still no errors).
Something else must be the problem, perhaps another installed package that, when loaded, interferes with the normal commands from package QCA.

I see you have a lot of packages attached (no less than 23). This is not a particularly good idea, because functions with the same names can be found in different packages and, depending which package you've loaded last, it will have precedence.

I'd say the script worked on R version 4.0.4 simply because you did not have the other packages installed and loaded.

Best,
Adrian

messages.body_plain:
If you want to get to the ground of this, Joanne, you could use your old setup and see whether the commands work when adding the package to the command: QCA::pof(conds, dummy.data$outcome). If it was a conflict of commands from different packages, it should disappear when specifying the package. You can switch between R versions in RStudio using Tools -> Global options -> General and choose from the R versions you have installed.

messages.body_plain:
That too, Ingo.
But function pof() uses other functions, some even from other packages, for instance compute() from package admisc and library dplyr has a similarly named one:

> library(QCA)
> library(dplyr)

Attaching package: ‘dplyr’

The following objects are masked from ‘package:admisc’:

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Re: Error: Object 'stms' not found
messages.body_plain:
To anyone interested, I've been exchanging a couple of more emails with Joanne.
The error seems to be related to the computer's locale, in her case Chinese Traditional, which uses a multi-byte character encoding.

After a couple of trials and errors, I seem to have found a workaround published in the latest development version of package admisc on GitHub.
But since this type of error is marginally affecting only a very small number of users, I will wait for a while until publishing a new official version on CRAN.

Best wishes, I hope this helps,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Data coercion issue
messages.body_plain:
Dear Wuraola,

Thank you for this message, but as stated in this working group description, to solve a particular problem needs a so-called MRE - minimal reproducible example.
Copy/paste-ing from the group description:

--------------------
Whenever you have a question about how to use a specific function or package, please construct a MRE (minimal reproducible example) that would include:
- a minimal dataset on which to apply your commands
- a minimal code that you have tried and did not yield the expected results
- the nature of the problem

Sometimes, issues might appear for different operating systems, versions of R and versions of the installed packages. When reporting an error, please test your example using the latest development version of the package from my website. If still reporting an error, please include the results from the following two R commands:
print(version)
sessionInfo()

Feel free to attach whatever you believe is relevant (.csv files, or R script files etc) all of your questions and answers will contribute to constructing an archive of potential topics that future users might be interested in.
--------------------

Best wishes,
Adrian

I have converted my data into fuzzy numbers but when I tried to run either the necessary or sufficiency analysis, I got a message that list cannot be coreced into type double. I read this QCA book written by you https://bookdown.org/dusadrian/QCAbook/Rbasics.html#data-coercion <https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbookdown.org%2Fdusadrian%2FQCAbook%2FRbasics.html%23data-coercion&data=04%...%40hanken.fi%7Cb902abd5f0c4458983b808d93aef68f3%7C6f304f3d06b9443c802a0606f683d043%7C0%7C0%7C637605622199509892%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C1000&sdata=fD9uSAiqprDH7aXClS7LVxn238kbtsthxv6i7T6ithg%3D&reserved=0> and realized you talked about issues like this and that it pertains to how R works.
